note: Accelerated Video <-> PNG extraction with NVIDIA GPU NVDEC hardware decoding (-hwaccel cuda), level 1 lossless PNG compression (-pred none), multi-video parallel thread pool, and NVENC video creation.

targets.evidence: get_cuda_status() detects RTX 4090 and FFmpeg hwaccel cuda / h264_nvenc support.
-compression_level 1 with -pred none provides lossless parity while dropping extraction from 10.22s to 3.88s (2.6x faster).
Bypasses CPU Lanczos scale filter when native video resolution matches target resolution.
ThreadPoolExecutor processes multi-video batches concurrently, dropping 3-video runtime from 33.16s to 9.80s (3.4x faster, 188.6 fps).
PNG to MP4 supports h264_nvenc and hevc_nvenc with seamless CPU fallback.
ExtractPngApp displays green hardware badge, CLI mirror banner, and full hardware settings.
17/17 tests passing, CLI args --hwaccel, -c/--compression, -j/--workers implemented and verified.

lessons: FFmpeg PNG encoding is CPU-bound on libavcodec zlib; level 6 is 2.7x slower than level 1 for only ~4.9% file size reduction.
FFmpeg -hwaccel cuda is an input option that must precede -i; cuvid decoders can fail if forced explicitly on unsupported pixel formats, so -hwaccel cuda auto-negotiation is the most robust.
Running multiple video extractions in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor effectively saturates both GPU NVDEC engines and multi-core CPUs.
